children: Utilities Sector Scorecard:
Sector Return: -13.01%
Best Performer: Constellation Energy
Worst Performer: PG&E
Top utility sector performers of the quarter
Despite the broader sector decline, only two utility stocks posted gains during the quarter. Constellation Energy
led the group, advancing 9.34% after signing a 20-year power agreement with Amazon that will support more than $3B of investment in its Calvert Cliffs nuclear plant.
Seeking Alpha analyst
said the deal also highlighted Constellation’s potential to play a larger role in meeting rising electricity demand from data centers.
AES Corporation
was the other gainer among the top-performing utility stocks, rising 2.26%.

Gerard highlighted that AES was the target of the transaction, with investors led by Global Infrastructure Partners and EQT Infrastructure VI agreeing to buy the company for $15/share in cash, at an enterprise value above $33B. PUCO’s approval for the change in control of AES Ohio was also a key regulatory step, although FERC approval is still required.
Gerard argued the rise in AES shares reflected a narrowing merger-arbitrage spread rather than a fundamental re-rating of the stock.
Here are the top gainers of the quarter:
Constellation Energy
: +9.34%, Quant rating: Hold with a score of 3.12 out of 5
AES Corporation
: +2.26%, Quant rating: Hold with a score of 3.02 out of 5
Top utility sector detractors of the quarter
On the downside, PG&E

was the biggest decliner, falling 29.35% during the quarter as uncertainty over wildfire liability reform weighed on the stock. UBS downgraded the utility to Neutral and lowered its price target to $14 from $19, citing the company’s decision to defer $2B in 2027 capital spending.

However, Gerard pointed out that PG&E still plans to spend $11.4B in 2027, while the same release reaffirmed its 2026 core EPS guidance of $1.64-$1.66 and introduced 2027 guidance of $1.78-$1.82. He added that the UBS downgrade reflected falling odds of wildfire reform this year after California Gov. Gavin Newsom floated a special session focused on AI rather than wildfire reform.
Edison International

also fell 29.32% during the quarter, facing the same California wildfire liability concerns that weighed on PG&E. Gerard cited the stock’s 23% drop on Aug. 31, its worst single-day decline in more than 25 years, after Senate Bill 492 excluded the liability protections investors had expected. WCF and Mizuho downgraded the stock that day, while Fitch later cut its outlook on the company.
He also mentioned that a jury trial related to the Eaton Fire is scheduled for January 2027.
NRG Energy

also ended the quarter lower, declining 29.00%. As an independent power producer, NRG was less exposed to the broader rate-hike narrative, Gerard said. The stock had already fallen 8% in July and fell further following its Q2 EPS miss, which reflected higher interest and other costs from its LS Power assets. Gerard cited investor caution over weaker Texas power prices as another factor weighing on the stock.
Here are the top five detractors of the quarter:

: -29.35%, Quant rating: Hold with a score of 2.98 out of 5
